messages.subject: how to convert excel file to genind
messages.subject_clean: how to convert excel file to genind
messages.body_plain:
Hi to all
I am trying to read excel file into R and then trying transpose and trying to convert it to Genind object
I am almost successfull in reading data into R, but i am getting this error while converting to Genind object
Error in dimnames(x) <- dn :
  length of 'dimnames' [1] not equal to array extent

can any one help to solve out this problem? any help in this regard is highly appreciated
My code and example data file is here
data - https://www.dropbox.com/s/4qtsqme6b6v3fha/example.xlsx?dl=0
code - https://www.dropbox.com/s/hg11swjhzjrvsvv/code.txt?dl=0
Thanks in advance
Regards,

messages.subject_clean: [poppr] how to convert excel file to genind
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

The problem you are having is due to two things:

1. the `t()` function converts the data to a matrix, which means that f[[1]] returns "M1"
2. your locus names are in the first row

Only potentially problematic: you are removing the first two columns of your data when you have no need to. Below I've posted a reproduction of the problem and the solution. Note that I'm using readxl here because I find it easier to handle.

library("poppr")
#> Loading required package: adegenet
#> Loading required package: ade4
#>
#>    /// adegenet 2.1.2 is loaded ////////////
#>
#>    > overview: '?adegenet'
#>    > tutorials/doc/questions: 'adegenetWeb()'
#>    > bug reports/feature requests: adegenetIssues()
#> This is poppr version 2.8.1. To get started, type package?poppr
#> OMP parallel support: available
fp <- "~/Downloads/example.xlsx"
(a <- readxl::read_excel(fp))
#> # A tibble: 9 x 6
#>   INDIVIDUAL IND1  IND2  IND3  IND4  IND5
#>   <chr>      <chr> <chr> <chr> <chr> <chr>
#> 1 M1         TT    TT    TT    TT    TT
#> 2 M2         CC    CC    GG    CC    CC
#> 3 M3         GG    GG    AA    AA    GG
#> 4 M4         GG    GG    GG    GG    GG
#> 5 M5         GG    GG    GG    GG    GG
#> 6 M6         CC    CC    TT    CC    CC
#> 7 M7         CC    AA    CC    CC    CC
#> 8 M8         TT    TT    CC    TT    TT
#> 9 M9         AA    AA    AA    AA    AA
(f <- t(a))
#>            [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] [,6] [,7] [,8] [,9]
#> INDIVIDUAL "M1" "M2" "M3" "M4" "M5" "M6" "M7" "M8" "M9"
#> IND1       "TT" "CC" "GG" "GG" "GG" "CC" "CC" "TT" "AA"
#> IND2       "TT" "CC" "GG" "GG" "GG" "CC" "AA" "TT" "AA"
#> IND3       "TT" "GG" "AA" "GG" "GG" "TT" "CC" "CC" "AA"
#> IND4       "TT" "CC" "AA" "GG" "GG" "CC" "CC" "TT" "AA"
#> IND5       "TT" "CC" "GG" "GG" "GG" "CC" "CC" "TT" "AA"
snps <- df2genind(f[, -c(1, 2)],
                  ind.names = f[[1]],
                  ploidy = 2,
                  sep="")
#> Error in dimnames(x) <- dn: length of 'dimnames' [1] not equal to array extent
snps <- df2genind(f[-1, ],
                  loc.names = f[1, ],
                  ploidy = 2,
                  ncode = 1,
                  sep = ""
                  )
genind2df(snps)
#>      M1 M2 M3 M4 M5 M6 M7 M8 M9
#> IND1 TT CC GG GG GG CC CC TT AA
#> IND2 TT CC GG GG GG CC AA TT AA
#> IND3 TT GG AA GG GG TT CC CC AA
#> IND4 TT CC AA GG GG CC CC TT AA
#> IND5 TT CC GG GG GG CC CC TT AA
